Here the limits of the numerator and denominator are ${lim}_{x\to -\infty }{x}^{2}=\infty $ and ${lim}_{x\to -\infty }{e}^{-x}=\infty ,$ respectively, so we have the case $\frac{\infty }{\infty }.$

Applying L'Hopital's rule, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to -\infty }\frac{{x}^{2}}{{e}^{-x}} & ={lim}_{x\to -\infty }\frac{[{x}^{2}]^{′}}{{[{e}^{-x}]}^{′}} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to -\infty }\frac{2x}{-{e}^{-x}} \\  & =-{lim}_{x\to -\infty }\frac{2x}{{e}^{-x}}.\end{aligned}
$$

This time, the resulting limit gives the indeterminate form $\frac{-\infty }{\infty }.$ To find the limit, we apply L'Hopital's rule once again. We get

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to -\infty }\frac{{x}^{2}}{{e}^{-x}} & =-{lim}_{x\to -\infty }\frac{2x}{{e}^{-x}} \\  & =-{lim}_{x\to -\infty }\frac{[2x]^{′}}{[{e}^{-x}]^{′}} \\  & =-{lim}_{x\to -\infty }\frac{2}{-{e}^{-x}} \\  & =2{lim}_{x\to -\infty }{e}^{x} \\  & =0.\end{aligned}
$$
